description:
Add, remove, or list a note's tags. Defaults to the frontmatter `tags:` array — set `location` to `inline` or `both` to mutate the note body. `add` ensures the tag is present in the requested location(s); `remove` strips it; `both` reconciles across both representations. Inline `#tag` detection skips what Obsidian indexes no tag in: code (fenced, indented, and inline), wikilinks (`[[...]]` — so a heading anchor, block anchor, or wikilink alias is never read as a tag or rewritten by a removal), images, a markdown link's destination or label (its text is read), HTML blocks and comments (``), and math (`$…$`, `$$…$$`). An inline tag starts at line start, after whitespace, after another tag (`#a#b` is two tags), or right after markup such as `**`, `_…_`, `==`, `[`, a table cell's `|`, `
`, or a `\`-escape (`**#x**` is a tag; `(#x`, `a *#x`, and `\#x` are not); a `#` inside a `%% … %%` comment still counts. Inline-location additions append the new tag at end-of-file. `list` ignores the input `tags` array.

location.description: Where to apply the change. Defaults to `frontmatter` (the canonical Obsidian tag location, leaves the body untouched). `inline` mutates the note body — `add` appends `#tag` at end-of-file. `both` is opt-in reconciliation of frontmatter and inline tag locations.

operation.description: `add` and `remove` mutate the note; `list` reads the current tag set.

tags.description: Tags to add or remove. Omit the leading `#`. Required for add/remove.

oneOf.description: Address a note by its vault-relative path.
Address whichever file is currently active in the Obsidian UI.

type.description: Address the file currently open in Obsidian.

oneOf.description: Address a periodic note (current or dated).

date.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for the current period.

name: obsidian_manage_tags

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `path_forbidden`: `list` requires the path to be readable; `add`/`remove` require it to be inside OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, with OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=false. `tags_required`: `operation` is "add" or "remove" but `tags` was empty or omitted. `frontmatter_invalid`: `location` reaches the frontmatter and the note's existing block does not parse as a mapping of properties, or the tag change would leave YAML that cannot be re-emitted. Nothing is written — the note keeps its original bytes, and under `location: "both"` the inline half is skipped too rather than applied on its own. `note_missing`: The vault path does not resolve to an existing note. `no_active_file`: Target was `active` but no file is currently open in Obsidian. `periodic_unsupported`: Target was `periodic` and this vault runs Local REST API v5.0.2 or later without the companion periodic-notes extension, so the `/periodic/` routes are not served at all. `periodic_not_found`: Target was `periodic`, the `/periodic/` routes are served on this vault, and no note exists for the requested period. `periodic_disabled`: Target was `periodic` but the requested period is not enabled in Obsidian's Periodic Notes plugin settings. `path_is_directory`: The supplied path names a folder rather than a note file. `path_traversal`: The path contains a `.` or `..` segment, which is rejected to prevent vault escape. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

tags.description: Tags split by location plus the deduplicated union.

all.description: Deduplicated union of frontmatter and inline tags.

applied.description: Tags actually changed by this call.

currentSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note after the add. Equals `previousSizeInBytes` when no tags were applied.

previousSizeInBytes.description: Byte size of the note before the add.

skipped.description: Tags already present at the targeted location(s).
